transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Chinese President Xi is continuing his state visit to the U.S.
President Trump held a state dinner for him at the White House last night.
That followed their day of meetings.
Neither Xi nor Trump directly answered questions about whether Taiwan came up during their
discussions.
But as Ashish Valentine reports from Taipei, Taiwan is emphasizing its right to self-determination.
Following the full day of meetings between Xi and President Trump, China's Ministry
of Foreign Affairs released their readout of Xi Jinping's remarks.
Xi reportedly expressed hope that the U.S. would oppose Taiwan independence and handle
the Taiwan issue prudently.
Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded to Xi's remarks in a statement, saying Taiwan's
future can only be decided through democratic means.
Taiwan's President Lai Qingde said in a speech last week that faced with the escalating threat
from China.
His responsibility is to ensure Taiwan is better prepared.
Part of that agenda, he said, is raising defense spending to 5 percent of GDP by 2030.
From NPR News, I'm Ashish Valentine in Taipei.
With the November midterm elections less than six weeks away, more Republicans are distancing
themselves from President Trump.
NPR's Elena Moore says the GOP is seeking to hold onto a slim majority in Congress,
amid the president's low approval ratings.
A handful of Republicans are breaking with Trump on key issues, like the war with Iran.
This week, multiple Senate candidates running in competitive races called for the conflict
to end, including Mike Rogers in Michigan.
Michigan families are struggling with the price of everyday life.
Groceries cost too much.
We have to bring prices down.
The war with Iran needs to end and end quickly.
Trump's been looming large throughout this midterm cycle, and he's repeatedly told supporters
to vote like he's on the ballot.
But that could hurt his party.
According to the latest NPR/PBS News/Marist poll, a plurality of registered voters, 45
percent, say they're voting against him.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered his remarks yesterday to the U.N.
General Assembly.
Many other world leaders this week have sharply criticized his government.
NPR's Cat Lonsdorf reports Netanyahu has responded to the criticism.
He downplayed settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, saying it was the
work of 150 juvenile delinquents.
The U.K. recently said such settler attacks and land grabs amount to, quote, "ethnic cleansing."
Netanyahu rejected claims that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza, something that's
come up repeatedly from other world leaders this week.
He also accused the media of not telling the "truth" about what's happening in Gaza.
But just a reminder, Israel has not allowed outside journalists to enter Gaza to independently
report in almost three years the entirety of this war.
NPR's Cat Lonsdorf.
This is NPR.
Mortgage rates for a standard home loan are now more than 7 percent.
Only two weeks ago, the rate was about six and three quarters.
Analysts say the war in Iran is a driving reason for the big jump.
It's because it's boosted the cost of oil and inflation that, in turn, creates volatility
in the bond market, affecting the cost of borrowing.
Pope Leo is in the midst of a day-long series of speeches across France that began in the
French capital.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports Leo's four-day trip is the first official papal visit to
France since 2008.
French television is covering the Pope's visit live, showing him being greeted by President
Macron, officers of the French military, and dozens of schoolchildren on a red carpet on
the airport tarmac as he stepped off his plane.
In an opening speech to Macron and diplomats at the Elize Palace, Leo raised existential
questions about scientific progress, life, and human rights.
He warned that a "paradise of machines" risks undermining humanity.
The Pope will greet the faithful in the streets of Paris before heading to Notre Dame Cathedral.
This evening, he is holding a sold-out mass at the Stade de France, Paris' major sports
stadium.
There is huge fervor for his visit in a country that's both traditionally Catholic and staunchly
secular.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre Nou's Paris.
The outer bands of Hurricane NOLO are starting to reach the big island of Hawaii.
A hurricane watches up.
Forecasters don't think the storm will make landfall, but it is a big rainmaker.
Nearly two feet of rain could fall on parts of Hawaii.
This is NPR.

Taiwan emphasizes right to self-determination in response to Xi's remarks during Trump meetings
Taiwan President Lai pledges to raise defense spending to 5 percent of GDP by 2030
Republicans distance themselves from Trump ahead of November midterm elections seeking to hold Congress
Michigan Senate candidate Mike Rogers calls for end to war with Iran during campaign
NPR/PBS poll shows 45 percent of voters plan to vote against Trump in midterms
Israeli PM Netanyahu downplays settler violence as work of 150 juvenile delinquents at U.N.
Netanyahu rejects genocide accusations in Gaza, criticizes media coverage of conflict
Mortgage rates jump above 7 percent due to Iran war impact on oil and inflation

Pope holds sold-out mass at Stade de France stadium in Paris during visit
